clue.text: Channel surfer's original characteristic

indicators.note: original means the first, so the opening letter of surfer's is taken

parts.note: a characteristic is a trait

explanation.surface: A sea-lover's defining quality, linked to the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow sea passage, the same thing as a channel of water.

clue.text: Watercolour?

parts.note: read not as a painting medium but as a picture whose colour and subject is the water of the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A painting of the sea is a picture of water, so a playful sense of watercolour.

clue.text: One tells of motorists planning route over the pole

parts.note: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

indicators.note: planning a route suggests working the letters of route into a new order

parts.note: N stands for the north pole

explanation.surface: A driving club plans a journey across the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planning' rearranges ROUTE with N to give ONTEUR; 'over' only links. The RAC is Britain's Royal Automobile Club, a motoring breakdown organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a storyteller, someone who recounts anecdotes.

clue.text: Guesses that Eskimos welcome temperature

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the Inuit people, here pluralised

explanation.surface: Arctic people greet the cold with a hunch.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit is to sense or guess something without reasoning.

clue.text: Caution a very attractive girl covering half a day

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: a dish is slang for a very attractive person

indicators.note: half means keeping only one half of the word Monday, dropping the rest

parts.note: Monday is a day of the week

explanation.surface: Warning a glamorous woman who works only a morning shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' trims MONDAY to MON, which A DISH is 'covering' to give AD-MON-ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish is to warn or reprimand someone, a synonym of caution as a verb.

clue.text: Cheating at duplicate bridge?

definitions.meaning: crossing over a second span, a doubled bridge crossing

explanation.definitionFit: Treachery is betrayal; humorously it also means going over two spans.

clue.text: River of gold — one with no cobalt!

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
Co is the chemical symbol for cobalt

explanation.surface: A gold-bearing river that lacks the metal cobalt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is a major watercourse of Venezuela in South America.

clue.text: Chemical compound found in one explosive device

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a mine is a buried bomb

explanation.surface: A chemical turns up inside a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: An imine is an organic substance containing a carbon-nitrogen double bond.

clue.text: Singles in hotel — time to be frank!

indicators.note: in places one piece within another

parts.note: H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet
singles are ones

explanation.surface: A hotel guest admits it is time to be candid about single rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frank means being candid and truthful.

clue.text: Supporters of lines of communication

parts.note: posts that hold up the overhead wires carrying messages, not people backing a cause

explanation.definitionFit: Tall wooden posts hold aloft the cables used for wired messaging.

clue.text: A way to protect company's racy venue

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A road guards a firm's racy location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racy' is a pun: Ascot is a famous English racecourse, not a risqué spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a Berkshire racecourse, a venue for horse races.

clue.text: Learning to ride out in formation

indicators.note: formation suggests the letters being arranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Learning to ride out alongside others in formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formation' rearranges RIDE, OUT and IN; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep scholarship gained by study.

clue.text: Place limits on prisoner in good health

parts.note: con is slang for a convict
fine means well

explanation.surface: Restricting an inmate who is feeling well.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine is to restrict or keep within bounds.

clue.text: Left one single ship for this animal

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
single means one
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: Someone abandons one lone boat for a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A lioness is a female big cat, an animal.

clue.text: Following stress the chef goes to pot!

definitions.text: Following stress the chef goes to pot!

parts.words: Following stress the chef goes to pot!
parts.note: read as a cook cracking under strain, but really a kitchen pot that cooks under steam stress

explanation.definitionFit: This sealed pan cooks food fast using high steam force.

clue.text: Being sixteen, upset before church

indicators.note: before puts the reordered letters ahead of the church abbreviation
upset means knocked about, so the letters of sixteen are reordered

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A sixteen-year-old in a state before church.
explanation.definitionFit: Being and existence both mean the state of living.

clue.text: Dine out on American cash, it's obscene!

indicators.note: out means put out of shape, so the letters of dine are rearranged

parts.note: a cent is a US coin

explanation.surface: Dining out on a few dollars is called shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DINE to INDE; 'on' links it to CENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent means offensive to decency, rude or lewd.

clue.text: Before job accepting drink — that's an assumption!

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the drink sits inside the other letters

parts.note: pre means before
a position is a job
sup means drink

explanation.surface: Taking a drink before work: what a guess!
explanation.definitionFit: A presupposition is something taken for granted in advance.

clue.text: Politician, foreign chap, drinking a tea noisily

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: senor is Spanish for a man
taken as written

indicators.note: noisily means as spoken, so the word tea is heard as a letter

parts.note: tea sounds like the letter T

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman slurps his tea loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noisily' makes TEA the letter T; with A it goes inside SENOR via 'drinking'.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is an elected member of an upper legislative house.

clue.text: The laziness of a single functional retina?

parts.note: a single is one, I as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: functional suggests the retina being made to work, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Is one working retina lazy?
explanation.walkthrough: 'functional' rearranges RETINA to NERTIA, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia means sluggishness, a tendency to remain inactive.

clue.text: An insect watched her, listening

indicators.note: listening means as heard, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: watched her means spied her

explanation.surface: A creature that observed her while eavesdropping.
explanation.walkthrough: A spider is strictly an arachnid, not an insect; the setter uses the loose everyday sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosely, a spider is a creepy-crawly, popularly lumped with bugs.

clue.text: Regular bargain at the greengrocer's?

parts.note: par is the normal or regular level
snip is British slang for a bargain

explanation.surface: A good deal at the fruit and veg shop.
explanation.walkthrough: SNIP is British slang for a bargain; the definition is a whimsical 'something sold at the greengrocer's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsnips are root vegetables sold by a vegetable seller.

clue.text: Right, step up and summarise!

parts.note: R is right

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a pace is a step

explanation.surface: An order to step up and sum up.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to restate the main points briefly.

clue.text: Staff must command respect

indicators.note: command means order, so the letters of respect are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Employees must earn respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like workers; it is a rod of office.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre is a ceremonial rod carried by a monarch.

clue.text: Singular events — led on with chat, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that these letters might be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Unique happenings encouraged by talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular events' means a single contest of ten events, not unusual happenings.
explanation.definitionFit: A decathlon is one athletics contest made of ten events.

clue.text: Can good English provide a hint?

parts.note: a tin is a can
G is good
E is English

explanation.surface: Asking whether a decent Englishman can offer a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace, a hint of colour or quality.

clue.text: Order a new couch?

parts.note: couch read as a verb meaning to word something, so to express it again in other terms, not buy a sofa

explanation.definitionFit: To couch is to express in words, so doing it afresh means saying it differently.

clue.text: Warning queen to accept greeting from Rome

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a queen is a female cat
ave is Latin for hail

explanation.surface: A monarch receives a salute from Rome as a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a caution or proviso.
